title: own scope targeting the OWNED entity, in a manifest that also declares an unowned one
coversRequirement: AZ7 positive #6 (over-rejection guard, structural twin of negative #4)
why: The manifest declares two entities: 'Widget', which declares ownershipField 'created_by', and 'Setting', which declares no ownership relation because a settings row has no owner and must not be forced to invent one. The own-scope Action targets 'Widget' — the entity that actually carries ownership. This is legitimate and must install. Most entities have no ownership concept, so a manifest mixing owned and unowned entities is the normal case, not a suspicious one.
notes: THE DECISIVE PAIR. This fixture is byte-for-byte the same shape as az7-n4 apart from WHICH entity the Action targets: n4 targets the unowned one and must be REJECTED, p2 targets the owned one and must be ACCEPTED. A validator that rejects both is banning unowned entities rather than enforcing the per-entity rule; a validator that accepts both has not implemented AZ7 at all and CWE-863 is still open. Run these two together, always, and report them together. Like n4, the decision is a cross-array join and therefore a VALIDATOR obligation — the schema accepts both, correctly, and that accept is not a schema defect.
